text: Air pollution has consequences similar to those of Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) and COVID-19. In 2023, air pollution accounted for over 2 million deaths in India. Of the Rs 13,415 crore allocated under the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) to control air pollution, around 68% has gone to road-dust management, 14% towards transport, and 12% towards waste management and biomass burning, without any appreciable improvement. Success cannot be measured by fund allocation and announced restrictions, but by actual reductions in population exposure and improvements in health through mission-mode, coordinated implementation by the environment, health, transport, power, agriculture, and urban development ministries, as during COVID. Air pollution is far more than a respiratory health concern; it contributes to cardiovascular disease, stroke, chronic respiratory disorders, lung cancer and diabetes. @CAQM_Official  @moefcc @MoHFW_INDIA @MORTHIndia @MinOfPower @AgriGoI @MoHUA_India @PMOIndia

title: Association between sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors and the risk of chronic lower respiratory disease in type 2 diabetes mellitus: findings from two target trial emulations.
text: BACKGROUND: Research on the association between sodium‑glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT-2i) and chronic lower respiratory diseases (CLRDs) in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2DM) remains limited. This study aimed to investigate this association and examine the potential modifying effects such as age, sex, and diabetes severity. METHODS: Using the Shenzhen Public Health Data Platform, we conducted two independent target trial emulations with a new‑user active comparator design, comparing SGLT‑2i with glucagon‑like peptide‑1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA) and dipeptidyl peptidase‑4 inhibitors (DPP‑4i), respectively. The primary outcome was incident CLRD; secondary outcomes included five subtypes-bronchitis, bronchiectasis, asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and emphysema. Overlap-weighted Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 1.76 years, 349 (7.95%) and 397 (9.04%) new CLRD cases occurred in SGLT-2i and GLP-1RA users, respectively. Compared with GLP-1RA, SGLT-2i use was associated with a lower CLRD incidence (HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.79-0.96), primarily driven by reduced risk of bronchitis (HR: 0.89; 95% CI: 0.79-1.00) and asthma (HR: 0.77; 95% CI: 0.58-1.01); no significant associations were found for other subtypes. Compared with DPP-4i, SGLT-2i use showed a trend toward lower CLRD risk (HR: 0.95; 95% CI: 0.91-0.99), with significant reductions for bronchitis (HR: 0.95; 95% CI: 0.91-1.00), bronchiectasis (HR: 0.86; 95% CI: 0.75-1.00), and asthma (HR: 0.87; 95% CI: 0.77-0.98). Subgroup analyses indicated significant interactions for bronchiectasis by sex (P interaction = 0.001). CONCLUSION: Compared with GLP-1 RA, SGLT-2i were associated with a significantly lower risk of CLRDs, driven predominantly by bronchitis; versus DPP-4i, the risk reduction was primarily observed for bronchitis, bronchiectasis, and asthma. The protective association between SGLT-2i use and bronchiectasis was more pronounced in females than in males relative to DPP-4i.
